name: Wild Rabbit (General Habitat)
description: The wild rabbit is the most common native mammal across San Andreas. Spawns naturally in Vinewood Hills, Mount Chiliad, Paleto Forest, and Tongva Valley.
features: Target animal for Wildlife Photography Challenge
Common throughout hilly and brush vegetation
Fast-moving and easily scared by footsteps or vehicles
income: Photograph target for Kraken Submersible reward

name: White-Tailed Deer / Doe
description: Herds of deer grazing along the wooded slopes of Mount Chiliad and Paleto Forest. Trevor's classic hunting prey.
features: Trevor hunting missions and photography challenge
Dense population in the northern boreal forests
Flees immediately at any gunshot or noise

name: Mountain Lion / Cougar
description: The deadliest land apex predator in San Andreas. Stalks the rocky ravines and attacks by surprise with lethal speed.
features: Aggressive apex predator with a one-hit kill bite
Distinctive low growls before pouncing
Photographable from a safe distance

name: Desert Coyote
description: Wild desert canine scavenger typical of the Grand Senora Desert and Sandy Shores Airfield surroundings.
features: Howls across the desert plains at night
Roams solo or in pairs near rural roads
Less aggressive than cougars, runs from vehicles

name: Wild Boar
description: Stout wild boar foraging in the scrub hills surrounding Bolingbroke Penitentiary and Senora National Park.
features: Powerful charge if startled or cornered
Common in dry brush and cactus clusters
Wildlife photography target

name: Red-Tailed Hawk
description: Raptor gliding on thermal currents high above the iconic Vinewood Sign and the Galileo Observatory.
features: Majestic circular soaring flight pattern
Sharp high-pitched screech audible from below
Perches on boulders, fences, and power poles

name: Neotropical Cormorant
description: Dark-feathered waterfowl diving for fish in the shallow estuaries and swampland of Lago Zancudo.
features: Common along wetlands, rivers, and coastal inlets
Dries plumage with outstretched wings on rocks
Official wildlife photography entry

name: Silver Gull / Seagull
description: Ubiquitous coastal bird wheeling above Del Perro Pier boardwalk and the busy beaches of Vespucci.
features: Perches on pier handrails and the Ferris wheel
Extremely easy to spot and photograph on the sand
Quick photo target

name: Great White Shark
description: Apex ocean predator patrolling deep coastal waters. Will breach, attack inflatable boats, and devour unprotected divers.
features: Supreme marine predator with unique kill animations
Appears as an active red blip on the minimap in deep water
Photographable safely from watercraft

name: Farm Cow & Pig
description: Domestic livestock grazing in the agricultural corrals of Grapeseed at the base of Mount Chiliad.
features: Both farm species located in the same Grapeseed pens
Completely harmless and simple to photograph
Idyllic rural setting

name: Pacific Dolphin
description: Intelligent and playful marine mammal. Swims and leaps in small pods in the open coastal waters off Pacific Bluffs and Chumash.
features: Playful aquatic mammal leaping across the water surface
Visible in pods across open ocean swells
Playable animal via underwater peyote plants in Story Mode

name: Orca / Killer Whale
zone: Northern High Seas (El Gordo Lighthouse & Mt. Chiliad)
description: The largest predatory cetacean off the shores of San Andreas. Glides through deep waters and surfaces to breach with unmistakable black-and-white patterns.
features: Massive oceanic mammal swimming in northern deep waters
Iconic marine species visible offshore
Controllable animal via underwater peyote plant in Story Mode
